history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Build buggy and fixed pandas (same compiled recipe, same interpreter) so that the developer test selection (the eight named cases, run via -k with the file path) fails on buggy with a real assertion failure and passes on fixed. Adjust only the build/environment, never the test.
assumptions: Python version 3.11 is inferred (pandas 3.x era supports 3.11+); the context does not state an interpreter and PR date is null.
No numpy/pandas pin is applied because the context gives no documented era ceiling; NEP 50 behaviour is assumed to come from the default NumPy 2.x resolution.

The native_library_failure diagnosis is taken as a hint that the compiled build is the risk point; the specific compiler error is unknown until the rebuild runs, so a pin or build-config change may be needed in a later iteration.
The -k expression lists all eight named cases so one run covers the transition; the test file path is included as required.

actions.step: Rebuild buggy revision as a compiled package (pandas has Cython extensions; installation_commands use pip install . / editable no-build-isolation build) on CPython 3.11, with no dependency pins since no era constraint is documented.
Rebuild fixed revision identically (same recipe, same interpreter) so the comparison is like for like.
Run the developer test selection on buggy: expect FAIL with an assertion mismatch (wrong row label / position for uint64 above 2**53 and tie cases), not a collection or import error.
